text:
claire: opened PR #5588 to add Apex9b model card clarifications: embedding throughput guidance, recommended batching for high-traffic embed pipelines, and a small fix to the cURL example that was sending the wrong Content-Type. preview: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5588

diego: nice. quick Q: are we documenting the per-minute embedding quotas as well? SEs keep hitting rate limits in prod when they naive-batch.

claire: yes, plan is: add a short section "Embedding throughput & rate limits" with a recommended batching table (batch sizes vs expected latency/throughput on A100 and V100) and a note to request quota increases for sustained traffic.

anika: can you paste the bench numbers you have? i can format a tiny table. also flagging that SDK v4 prefers `batch_size` in the embeddings helper vs older `num_inputs` names. docs should use the v4 param.

claire: raw numbers from quick run on a single A100 (batch=1 clients, synthetic inputs):
- batch=1: 48 qps, median latency 21ms
- batch=8: 320 qps, median latency 28ms
- batch=32: 1200 qps, median latency 75ms
CSV + plot uploaded: https://drive.google.com/apex9b-embed-bench.csv and https://drive.google.com/apex9b-embed-plot.png

morgan: nit: the PR's cURL example used single quotes and didn't set Content-Type: application/json (bash on some CI shells chokes). i'll add a corrected cURL snippet and a small SDK v4 example.

dan: (joining thread briefly) also add a one-line compatibility note: some low-memory quantized embed variants offload on-the-fly which increases tail latency for large batches. put this under "Compatibility" so customers know why throughput numbers vary.

anika: suggested SDK v4 snippet (js):
```js
const embeddings = await client.embeddings.create({
  model: "apex9b",
  input: texts,
  batch_size: 32, // v4 param
});
```

claire: added the SDK snippet. updated the bench table wording: "observed on single A100 (p4d-equivalent), synthetic 768-dim embeddings" and clarified this is representative; your mileage may vary on CPU/offload setups.

morgan: here's the corrected cURL for the migration section (in PR now):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"apex9b","input":["hello","world"]}'
```

dan: tiny nit: recommend adding an explicit "per-minute quota" link to /pricing/quotas and a one-line example of how to programmatically exponential-backoff. SEs love that.

claire: added a small "rate-limit guidance" box with recommended backoff and a link to /pricing/quotas. also included a tiny Python retry snippet.

docbot: docs-lint: failed \u001F2b0 - bench CSV link points to personal drive path. please host under internal /benchmarks/embeddings/apex9b or use the public bench bucket.

claire: ack, moving CSV to the internal bench bucket and updating link. pushing update.

morgan: reviewed the cURL and SDK snippets, left one tiny nit about escaping in the markdown. otherwise LGTM.

anika: left a nit about calling out `batch_size` tradeoffs: higher batch sizes increase throughput but also tail latency under memory pressure. i added a one-line under "Tradeoffs".

claire: updated tradeoffs line and swapped the CSV link to /benchmarks/embeddings/apex9b.csv. preview: https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/5588/

docbot: docs-lint: passed \u2705 preview: https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/5588/ (staging)

morgan: +1

anika: +1

diego: left one small request: add a tiny FAQ entry "How do I pick batch_size for streaming pipelines?" with short guidance.

claire: good idea, added FAQ with recommended default batch_size=8 for low-latency streaming and batch_size>=32 for high-throughput offline indexing. also added a note for Dedicated customers: pin a variant and run the bench script in /tools/bench to reproduce.

dan: +1

claire: merging after CI green. follow-up: create a short internal note for support with the bench CSV and a recommended template to help customers request quota increases. thanks all! :shipit:
